title: Revisiting Nonstationary Kernel Design for Multi-Output Gaussian Processes
claim: A simpler stationary-style baseline fits nonstationary, input-dependent data poorly in smooth regions, motivating more flexible kernels.
layout: 2 side-by-side plot panels, shared legend strip below, overlaid model fits
description: Two side-by-side line plots of regression fits on one-dimensional data, with a shared legend row beneath. Panel (a), labeled 'Periodic function', shows rapidly oscillating black training dots whose amplitude and frequency change across the input range. A blue line (MOHSM posterior mean) with a light blue 95% band overlays a red line (NG-SM posterior mean) with a pink band. The red curve tracks the dots closely, and the blue curve is smoother and loses the fast oscillations on the left. Panel (b), labeled 'Piecewise function', shows the same pattern: the red fit captures sharp oscillations and the blue fit is smoother. The eye goes first to the dense black dots and the red and blue curves with their shaded bands. The legend lists MOHSM, NG-SM, both confidence intervals and the training data.
caption: MOHSM vs. NG-SM fits on scalar observations. Panel (a) shows a periodic function, and panel (b) a piecewise function. In both panels, the blue line denotes the MOHSM posterior mean and the red line the NG-SM posterior mean. The shaded light blue and pink regions indicate the corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Black dots mark the training data.
abstract: Multi-output Gaussian processes (MOGPs) provide a Bayesian framework for modeling non-linear functions with multiple outputs, in which nonstationary kernels are essential for capturing input-dependent variations in observations. However, from a spectral (dual) perspective, existing nonstationary kernels inherit the inflexibility and over-parameterization of their spectral densities due to the restrictive spectral–kernel duality. To overcome this, we establish a generalized spectral–kernel duality that enables fully flexible matrix-valued spectral densities — albeit at the cost of quadratic parameter growth in the number of outputs. To achieve linear scaling while retaining sufficient expressiveness, we propose the multi-output low-rank nonstationary (MO-LRN) kernel: by modeling the spectral density through a low-rank matrix whose rows are independently parameterized by bivariate Gaussian mixtures. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that MO-LRN consistently outperforms existing MOGP kernels in regression, missing-data interpolation, and imputation tasks.
